question: Which feature of Spirogyra allows fragmentation to be successful?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Simple filamentous body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Spirogyra** is a genus of filamentous green algae found in freshwater environments such as ponds, ditches, and slow-moving streams.
 
• Its **simple filamentous structure** is composed of unbranched chains of cylindrical cells arranged end-to-end, which facilitates fragmentation.
 
• **Fragmentation** is an asexual reproduction method where each broken fragment of the filament can grow into a new individual under favorable conditions. This is possible due to the structural simplicity of Spirogyra.
 
• Unlike plants with complex tissues, Spirogyra lacks specialized tissues for transporting nutrients or water, which makes it highly adaptable to reproducing through fragmentation.
